title: As an AI-native user, I can point an agent at llms.txt or agent-oriented docs
As an AI-native user, I can run the product headlessly / in CI for automation
As an AI-native user, I can plug MCP servers into this product so it can use their tools
As an AI-native user, I can connect an agent via an official MCP server
As an AI-native user, I can use an official CLI
As an AI-native user, I can drive the product through a documented public API
As an AI-native user, I can issue scoped/least-privilege API credentials for an agent
As an AI-native user, I can build against official SDKs
As an AI-native user, I can subscribe to events via webhooks
As an AI-native user, I can get AI-generated insights and suggestions from my data inside the product
As an AI-native user, I can set up automations that run autonomously in the background
As an AI-native user, I can delegate tasks to a built-in AI assistant inside the product
As an AI-native user, I can operate the product with natural-language commands
As an AI-native user, I can explore an interactive API reference with runnable examples
As an AI-native user, I can download a machine-readable API spec (OpenAPI or equivalent)
As an AI-native user, I can test against a sandbox environment without touching production data
As an AI-native user, I can rely on versioned APIs with a documented deprecation policy
As an AI-native user, I can perform bulk operations across many items at once
As an AI-native user, I can define rules that trigger actions automatically on events
As an AI-native user, I can schedule recurring jobs or workflows
As an AI-native user, I can version, review, and roll back my automations
As a developer, seller-facing surfaces are embeddable — white-label components or APIs for balances, payouts, and transaction history that live inside my product under my brand
As a founder with offline sellers, in-person works on the same stack — terminals or tap-to-pay SDKs that settle into the same seller balances and reporting as online payments
As an ops user, sellers can self-serve their money questions — per-seller statements, payout reconciliation reports, and exports that let their bookkeeper close the month without contacting me
As a developer, funds can wait — hold seller funds in a balance until delivery or dispute windows pass, release on my schedule or trigger, with the escrow-like mechanics and their limits documented
As a finance lead, refunds and chargebacks that exceed a seller's balance are recoverable — automatic debits against future earnings or their bank account, with the liability order documented
As a developer, I can split one charge among any set of parties — route funds to multiple sellers, take my cut, and reverse or adjust the split later, all as first-class API objects

As an ops user, disputes are managed per seller — chargebacks land against the right sub-merchant, evidence is submitted via API or dashboard, and outcomes flow back into seller balances automatically
As an ops user, I can watch risk across my seller portfolio — fraud and credit-risk signals per sub-merchant, alerts on anomalous sellers, and tools to pause payouts or offboard bad actors
As a finance lead, international sellers get paid properly — local-currency payouts, documented FX handling, and settlement to local bank rails rather than expensive wires
As an ops user, payouts run on the schedule each seller needs — daily, weekly, monthly, or manual, plus instant payouts to cards or real-time rails where supported, configurable per seller
As an AI-native user, I can do everything through the API that I can do in the UI
As an AI-native user, I can export all of my data in open formats and leave
As an AI-native user, I can read the product's source under an open license
As an AI-native user, I can self-host the core product
As a founder, there's a path up the stack — start on the managed model and graduate toward registered payment facilitation with more economics and control, without replatforming

As an ops user, the responsibility split is explicit — who owns KYC/AML, card-network compliance, fraud losses, and seller misconduct between me and the provider, in the docs rather than the contract's fine print
As a finance lead, seller tax reporting is handled — 1099-K thresholds tracked, forms generated, delivered, and filed, with the data corrections workflow documented
As an AI-native user, an agent can work the money side — read balances and payouts, investigate a seller's missing payout, draft dispute evidence — against documented, agent-usable surfaces

As an AI-native user, an agent can run seller operations — create accounts, drive onboarding to completion, and answer requirements-due states through the API or an MCP surface with scoped credentials

As a developer, the platform is ready for agent buyers — documented support for agent-initiated checkout on marketplace transactions (agentic-commerce protocols, delegated payment credentials) that works with split funds flows
As a finance lead, platform funds have a home — clarity on where in-flight and held funds sit, whether balances earn yield, and how money is segregated from the provider's own accounts
As a finance lead, the platform's money is legible — balances by seller and by my own fee accounts, every movement traceable from charge through split to payout, reconcilable to the penny
As a developer, reconciliation is automatable — settlement and balance reports per seller and rolled up, delivered as files or APIs my finance stack consumes on schedule
As a founder, payments are a revenue line — take an application fee or markup on every transaction, set per-seller pricing, and see my payments revenue reported distinctly from processing costs
As a finance lead, I control the economics — a documented buy rate from the provider and freedom to set the sell rate my sellers see, with interchange-level cost visibility to manage the spread
As an AI-native user, I can choose where my data is stored (region/residency)
As an AI-native user, I can prevent my data from being used to train AI models
As an AI-native user, I can control data retention and deletion
As an AI-native user, I can opt out of telemetry and usage tracking
As a founder, sellers can join from where they are — supported onboarding countries, local payment methods, and local-currency settlement documented as a coverage map, not discovered ticket by ticket
As a developer, I can onboard a seller through the API — KYB and KYC, bank account linking, and terms acceptance — with hosted flows and embeddable components when I don't want to build the forms
As an ops user, onboarding friction is tunable — collect the minimum to start selling and gather the rest before payout thresholds, with clear requirements-due states per seller
